name: Introduction to simple circuits and switches

questions.q: What is required for an electric current to flow in a simple circuit?
a: A complete unbroken loop containing a power source and conducting path
An open switch and a non-conducting wire
Only a light bulb connected to nothing else
A source of sound energy and plastic threads

questions.q: What is the function of a cell or battery in an electrical circuit?
a: To block the flow of electrons completely
To provide the push (voltage/electrical energy) that drives the current
To consume all energy without transferring it
To measure the temperature of the wires

questions.q: Which of the following materials is a good electrical conductor commonly used to make wires?
What is the primary purpose of a switch in an electrical circuit?
a: To increase the weight of the circuit
To change the color of the connecting wires
To break or complete the circuit, controlling the flow of current

questions.q: What term is used for materials that do not allow electric current to pass through them easily?
What scientific instrument is used to measure electric current in a circuit?
What is the standard SI unit used to measure electric current?
In a series circuit containing a battery and two identical lamps, how is the current shared between the components?
a: The current splits into different values at each branch
The current is higher near the positive terminal
The current is the same at all points in the circuit

questions.q: What happens to the other lamp in a simple series circuit if one lamp breaks or is unscrewed?
a: The other lamp goes out because the circuit is broken
The other lamp shines twice as bright
The other lamp remains lit normally

questions.q: What is the main advantage of a parallel circuit over a series circuit for household lighting?
a: If one appliance breaks or is turned off, the other branches remain complete and stay lit
Parallel circuits only need one wire

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an electrical insulator used to cover metal wires for safety?
What effect does adding more batteries in series to a simple circuit have on a lamp?
a: The lamp stays exactly the same
The lamp becomes brighter due to increased voltage/current

questions.q: What happens to the brightness of two identical lamps connected in series compared to a single lamp with one battery?
a: The lamps are dimmer because the voltage is shared between them
One lamp is bright and the other is off

questions.q: Which circuit diagram symbol represents an open switch?
a: A line with a break and a raised lever showing a gap
A circle with a cross inside
Two parallel long and short lines

questions.q: What does a circle with a cross inside represent in a standard circuit diagram?
Why is copper chosen as the preferred metal for electrical wiring in homes and schools?
a: It is an excellent electrical conductor and flexible

questions.q: What is the role of a fuse or circuit breaker in a household electrical system?
a: To protect circuits and appliances by automatically breaking the flow if the current gets dangerously high
To slow down the flow of light
To convert electrical energy into sound

questions.q: In a parallel circuit, what can be said about the voltage across each parallel branch connected to the same power supply?
a: The voltage drops to zero in every branch
The voltage across each parallel branch is the same as the supply voltage
The voltage increases with each branch

questions.q: What will happen if you connect a wire directly from the positive terminal of a battery to the negative terminal without a component like a lamp (short circuit)?
a: The battery will charge up fully
The wire and battery will get dangerously hot very quickly

questions.q: Which of the following materials would allow a current to pass through it in a conductivity test?
How does adding more lamps in series to a circuit affect the overall current flowing from the battery?
a: The current decreases because total resistance increases

questions.q: What term describes the opposition to the flow of electric current offered by a component or wire?
If you have two identical lamps connected in parallel across a battery, how does their brightness compare to a single lamp circuit?
a: They are dimmer than a single lamp
They remain at normal full brightness because each branch connects directly to the supply

questions.q: Which scientist's unit of measurement is used for electrical resistance?
What is the standard symbol used to represent a cell in a circuit diagram?
a: One long parallel line and one short thick parallel line

questions.q: What is the purpose of drawing circuit diagrams using standard international symbols instead of realistic drawings?
a: To make circuits harder to build
To provide a universal, clear, and standardized way for scientists and engineers worldwide to communicate designs

questions.q: What happens in a parallel circuit if one branch contains a broken bulb while another branch has a working bulb?
a: The working bulb dims by half
